**Analysis of the test image:**

- **Affected plant part**: Green banana fruit (finger)
- **Visual features**:
  - Multiple discrete dark purple/black circular spots scattered across the fruit surface
  - One larger central lesion with a sunken, brownish fibrous center
  - Smaller spots appearing as dark dots with slightly raised or circular edges
  - Otherwise healthy green fruit skin

**Reasoning through each class:**

- **Anthracnose** (*Colletotrichum musae*): Classic presentation — dark, circular to slightly sunken lesions on banana fruit surface. Matches perfectly.
- **Cigar_End_Rot**: Affects only the distal tip of the fruit (tip rot), not scattered spots along the body.
- **Bunchy_Top**: Viral disease causing stunted whole-plant growth, dark streaks on leaf midribs — not fruit spots.
- **Cordana_Leaf_Spot**: Fungal disease affecting leaves with oval brownish lesions — not fruit.
- **Panama_Disease**: Vascular wilt disease causing leaf yellowing and pseudostem internal browning — not fruit spots.
- **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka**: Leaf diseases showing streaks/spots on leaf lamina — not fruit.

The scattered dark circular spots with a sunken center on the green banana fruit are the hallmark of **Anthracnose**, caused by *Colletotrichum musae*, which infects fruit both pre- and post-harvest.
